key_insight: Inverse PINNs can reliably estimate Manning friction in 2D shallow-water flows with moderate sparse/noisy data, but 1D cases show a persistent identifiability bias.
engineering_relevance: This benchmark clarifies when physics-informed inverse models are trustworthy for hydraulic parameter calibration from limited field observations.
method: Train a positive Manning friction scalar jointly with the flow field in a two-phase PINN scheme.
Test recovery under controlled changes in observation count, noise level, and observed variable type.
Compare a 1D MacDonald channel and a 2D sloped channel with a balanced finite-volume reference.
evidence_signal: In the 2D case, friction errors stayed below 5% with at least 10 depth and velocity observations and ≤10% noise, while the 1D case remained biased by about 15% regardless of data density.
watch_item: Do not assume more training data will fix poor identifiability: single-variable observations and the 1D setup can produce systematically biased friction estimates.
paper_title: How Sparse and How Noisy? Systematic Benchmarking of Inverse Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Manning Friction Estimation in Shallow Water Equations
